{
  "findings": [
    {
      "file": "pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go",
      "line": 51,
      "severity": "critical",
      "category": "concurrency",
      "title": "Async legacy writes derive from the request context and will be canceled when the request returns",
      "body": "In Create, the background goroutine creates a timeout context from the incoming request context: ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...). When the Create handler returns, the HTTP request context is normally canceled, so the derived context is canceled immediately and Legacy.Create will often fail with context canceled. This defeats the purpose of mode 3's asynchronous legacy write. The same pattern is used in Delete (line 110), Update (line 135), and DeleteCollection (line 163). A detached context, such as context.WithoutCancel or a background context carrying only logger/values, should be used for background writes."
    },
    {
      "file": "pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go",
      "line": 101,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Delete skips legacy deletion when unified delete returns NotFound",
      "body": "Delete returns immediately for any error from Storage.Delete, including NotFound. The previous mode 3 behavior explicitly tolerated NotFound from unified storage and still attempted Legacy.Delete. With this change, an object that exists only in legacy storage, or was removed from unified storage but not legacy storage, will never be deleted from legacy storage. This can leave stale legacy data that reappears if the system is rolled back to a mode that reads from legacy storage."
    },
    {
      "file": "pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go",
      "line": 139,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "Legacy update receives the original UpdatedObjectInfo instead of the object written to unified storage",
      "body": "Update passes the same rest.UpdatedObjectInfo to Storage.Update and later to Legacy.Update. Legacy.Update will therefore recompute the candidate object using the legacy store's current object, which may differ from the unified store's state. This can cause resource-version conflicts or write a different object to legacy storage than the one persisted in unified storage. The previous implementation wrapped the object returned by unified storage so that legacy storage received the exact resulting object; removing that breaks dual-write consistency."
    },
    {
      "file": "pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go",
      "line": 65,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "test_gap",
      "title": "Mode 3 unit tests do not wait for or assert asynchronous legacy writes",
      "body": "TestMode3_Create calls dw.Create and then asserts immediately, but the legacy write happens in a goroutine. The test does not synchronize with that goroutine or assert mock expectations, so it can pass even if Legacy.Create is never called, is called after the test finishes, or fails. The same issue exists for the Delete, Update, and DeleteCollection tests. These tests do not actually verify the asynchronous legacy-write behavior introduced by mode 3."
    },
    {
      "file": "pkg/tests/apis/playlist/playlist_test.go",
      "line": 132,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "test_gap",
      "title": "Mode 3 integration test asserts legacy state immediately after asynchronous writes",
      "body": "The new mode 3 subtest runs doPlaylistTests, which checks the legacy /api/playlists endpoints immediately after creating, updating, or deleting objects through the Kubernetes API. For example, it lists legacy playlists right after Kubernetes creates and calls getFromBothAPIs after updates. In mode 3, writes to legacy storage are asynchronous, so these assertions can race. The test should poll or otherwise wait for eventual consistency in mode 3, or avoid synchronous legacy assertions for asynchronous dual-write modes."
    },
    {
      "file": "pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go",
      "line": 106,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "perf",
      "title": "Delete success metric uses the resource name as the kind label",
      "body": "On successful Storage.Delete, the code records d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage). Elsewhere the third parameter is the resource kind, but here the object name is passed. This produces incorrect metric labels and can create high-cardinality metrics by putting per-resource names into a label intended to hold a kind. It should use the resource kind, such as options.Kind, consistently."
    },
    {
      "file": "pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go",
      "line": 166,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "DeleteCollection records legacy background duration as storage duration",
      "body": "In DeleteCollection's asynchronous goroutine, after calling d.Legacy.DeleteCollection, the code calls d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startLegacy). This attributes the legacy operation's duration and error status to unified storage metrics. It should call d.recordLegacyDuration instead."
    },
    {
      "file": "pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go",
      "line": 45,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Storage create failures are recorded as legacy durations",
      "body": "When d.Storage.Create fails, Create calls d.recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage). This attributes a unified-storage failure and duration to the legacy store, corrupting metrics. Update has the same issue at line 129, where a Storage.Update failure is recorded with recordLegacyDuration."
    },
    {
      "file": "pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go",
      "line": 56,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "Asynchronous legacy write failures are not logged or reconciled",
      "body": "In Create's background goroutine, the error from Legacy.Create is only passed to a metric; there is no logging, retry, queue, or reconciliation. If the legacy write fails because of timeout, conflict, or legacy-store outage, unified and legacy storage can silently diverge. The same fire-and-forget pattern exists in Delete, Update, and DeleteCollection. Since legacy writes are described as a safety measure, failures should at least be logged and ideally tracked or retried."
    },
    {
      "file": "pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go",
      "line": 50,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "concurrency",
      "title": "Background legacy writes are unordered and unbounded",
      "body": "Each write method launches an independent goroutine to update legacy storage. There is no per-resource sequencing, locking, queue, or concurrency limit. A fast sequence of create/update/delete operations can be applied to legacy storage out of order, for example a delete running before a create or an older update overwriting a newer one. This can leave legacy storage inconsistent even if every individual background call succeeds."
    },
    {
      "file": "pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go",
      "line": 97,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Delete puts the base logger into context instead of the enriched logger",
      "body": "Delete constructs log := d.Log.WithValues(\"name\", name, \"kind\", options.Kind, \"method\", method), but then sets ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log). Any logging inside Storage.Delete or Legacy.Delete that uses the context logger will miss the added name/kind/method values. The context should be set to log, not d.Log."
    },
    {
      "file": "pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go",
      "line": 113,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Benign legacy delete NotFound errors are counted as failures",
      "body": "In the asynchronous Delete path, any error returned by Legacy.Delete is recorded as a failure via d.recordLegacyDuration(err != nil, ...). If the object is already absent from legacy storage, NotFound is a benign condition, but it will be counted as a legacy error metric. The previous implementation ignored NotFound for legacy deletes; the new code should do the same for metrics and logging."
    }
  ]

findings.title: Async legacy writes derive from the request context and will be canceled when the request returns
findings.body: In Create, the background goroutine creates a timeout context from the incoming request context: ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...). When the Create handler returns, the HTTP request context is normally canceled, so the derived context is canceled immediately and Legacy.Create will often fail with context canceled. This defeats the purpose of mode 3's asynchronous legacy write. The same pattern is used in Delete (line 110), Update (line 135), and DeleteCollection (line 163). A detached context, such as context.WithoutCancel or a background context carrying only logger/values, should be used for background writes.

findings.title: Delete skips legacy deletion when unified delete returns NotFound
findings.body: Delete returns immediately for any error from Storage.Delete, including NotFound. The previous mode 3 behavior explicitly tolerated NotFound from unified storage and still attempted Legacy.Delete. With this change, an object that exists only in legacy storage, or was removed from unified storage but not legacy storage, will never be deleted from legacy storage. This can leave stale legacy data that reappears if the system is rolled back to a mode that reads from legacy storage.

findings.title: Legacy update receives the original UpdatedObjectInfo instead of the object written to unified storage
findings.body: Update passes the same rest.UpdatedObjectInfo to Storage.Update and later to Legacy.Update. Legacy.Update will therefore recompute the candidate object using the legacy store's current object, which may differ from the unified store's state. This can cause resource-version conflicts or write a different object to legacy storage than the one persisted in unified storage. The previous implementation wrapped the object returned by unified storage so that legacy storage received the exact resulting object; removing that breaks dual-write consistency.

findings.title: Mode 3 unit tests do not wait for or assert asynchronous legacy writes
findings.body: TestMode3_Create calls dw.Create and then asserts immediately, but the legacy write happens in a goroutine. The test does not synchronize with that goroutine or assert mock expectations, so it can pass even if Legacy.Create is never called, is called after the test finishes, or fails. The same issue exists for the Delete, Update, and DeleteCollection tests. These tests do not actually verify the asynchronous legacy-write behavior introduced by mode 3.

findings.title: Mode 3 integration test asserts legacy state immediately after asynchronous writes
findings.body: The new mode 3 subtest runs doPlaylistTests, which checks the legacy /api/playlists endpoints immediately after creating, updating, or deleting objects through the Kubernetes API. For example, it lists legacy playlists right after Kubernetes creates and calls getFromBothAPIs after updates. In mode 3, writes to legacy storage are asynchronous, so these assertions can race. The test should poll or otherwise wait for eventual consistency in mode 3, or avoid synchronous legacy assertions for asynchronous dual-write modes.

findings.title: Delete success metric uses the resource name as the kind label
findings.body: On successful Storage.Delete, the code records d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage). Elsewhere the third parameter is the resource kind, but here the object name is passed. This produces incorrect metric labels and can create high-cardinality metrics by putting per-resource names into a label intended to hold a kind. It should use the resource kind, such as options.Kind, consistently.

findings.title: DeleteCollection records legacy background duration as storage duration
findings.body: In DeleteCollection's asynchronous goroutine, after calling d.Legacy.DeleteCollection, the code calls d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startLegacy). This attributes the legacy operation's duration and error status to unified storage metrics. It should call d.recordLegacyDuration instead.

findings.title: Storage create failures are recorded as legacy durations
findings.body: When d.Storage.Create fails, Create calls d.recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage). This attributes a unified-storage failure and duration to the legacy store, corrupting metrics. Update has the same issue at line 129, where a Storage.Update failure is recorded with recordLegacyDuration.

findings.title: Asynchronous legacy write failures are not logged or reconciled
findings.body: In Create's background goroutine, the error from Legacy.Create is only passed to a metric; there is no logging, retry, queue, or reconciliation. If the legacy write fails because of timeout, conflict, or legacy-store outage, unified and legacy storage can silently diverge. The same fire-and-forget pattern exists in Delete, Update, and DeleteCollection. Since legacy writes are described as a safety measure, failures should at least be logged and ideally tracked or retried.

findings.title: Background legacy writes are unordered and unbounded
findings.body: Each write method launches an independent goroutine to update legacy storage. There is no per-resource sequencing, locking, queue, or concurrency limit. A fast sequence of create/update/delete operations can be applied to legacy storage out of order, for example a delete running before a create or an older update overwriting a newer one. This can leave legacy storage inconsistent even if every individual background call succeeds.

findings.title: Delete puts the base logger into context instead of the enriched logger
findings.body: Delete constructs log := d.Log.WithValues("name", name, "kind", options.Kind, "method", method), but then sets ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log). Any logging inside Storage.Delete or Legacy.Delete that uses the context logger will miss the added name/kind/method values. The context should be set to log, not d.Log.

findings.title: Benign legacy delete NotFound errors are counted as failures
findings.body: In the asynchronous Delete path, any error returned by Legacy.Delete is recorded as a failure via d.recordLegacyDuration(err != nil, ...). If the object is already absent from legacy storage, NotFound is a benign condition, but it will be counted as a legacy error metric. The previous implementation ignored NotFound for legacy deletes; the new code should do the same for metrics and logging.
